newsitem.title: UK: American Airlines warns U.K. on open skies - report.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines warns U.K. on open skies - report.

text.p: Britain will have to drop its insistence that foreign airlines be allowed to fly within the U.S. if it wants an "open skies" deal with Washington, American Airlines chairman Robert Crandall said.

In an interview with the Financial Times, Crandall said: "The issue is quite simple. Is the British government prepared to do an open skies agreement that essentially mirrors the deals that the US has done with other countries or is it not?"
Crandall said Britain should drop its "cabotage" demand that British carriers be allowed to carry passengers between U.S. cities.

"The U.S. government has signed these agreements with a substantial number of European countries: the Germans, the Dutch, the Austrians, the Belgians. The US government cannot do a deal with the U.K. government that is materially different from those transactions," he said.
"As a matter of realpolitik, if the US government did a different deal, the wheels would come off," he said.
Crandall has threatend to pull out of a proposed alliance with British Airways if the Anglo-American "open skies" talks drag on much longer.
